issues.description: The problem statement and the template Main refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name mismatch between specification/template and solution will confuse students about the required API and can break code/tests that expect acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent with the problem specification and template. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same signature (static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)), or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method name matches the problem statement and any tests/Main usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template's example call use the method name acceptSupplyDelivery(...) to represent receiving a stock delivery, but the solution implementation names this method receiveDelivery(...). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery and updating stock) can confuse students: they will look for acceptSupplyDelivery in the implementation and the provided example code/comments, but the solution defines receiveDelivery instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...), or alternatively update the problem statement and template example to call receiveDelivery(...). Preferably keep acceptSupplyDelivery(...) to match the problem description and the template's example usage.
